title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
claim: Uniform aggregation and standard preference losses treat unanimous and strongly disputed annotations alike; reliability-aware weighting resolves the disagreement.
layout: Stacked 2 rows plus bottom loss bar, left-to-right arrows, colored boxes
description: The figure has two stacked scenarios. The top blue panel, 'Unanimous Preference', shows five green smiley annotators all voting for Response A. The lower orange panel, 'Strong Disagreement', shows three smileys favoring Response A and two favoring Response B. Smileys with filled mouths mark high-reliability annotators, as the legend at top left explains. Brown arrows lead from each scenario to a gray 'Preference Pair' box. Each box has rows for Uniform Ensemble and RGPO, with green (winner, y_w) and tan (loser, y_l) tiles for A and B. In the disagreement case, Uniform Ensemble picks A, while RGPO flips to B because the reliable annotators prefer B. A bottom strip shows L_DPO in a blue box, a pink arrow labeled 'Consistency Weighting', and L_RGPO in a purple box with an added weight s̃. The eye goes first to the colored panels and smileys.
caption: Uniform Ensemble ignores the varying reliability levels of annotators, while existing RLHF frameworks such as DPO treat samples with strong disagreement identically to those with unanimous preference, thereby introducing potential inconsistency.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is critical for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences. However, its efficacy is often compromised by the inherent inconsistency and subjectivity of human annotations. Existing preference optimization frameworks, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), typically treat ambiguous pairs with high annotator disagreement identically to those with unanimous consensus, forcing models to overfit to inconsistent supervision signals and leading to suboptimal alignment. In this work, we propose Reliability-Guided Preference Optimization (RGPO), a robust framework designed to mitigate the impact of inconsistent human feedback. RGPO estimates annotator reliability and infers latent ground truth labels from noisy human feedback to identify robust preferences. Furthermore, we introduce a reliability-aware consistency optimization that dynamically modulates the training objective based on the consensus level of annotations, ensuring the model prioritizes high-consensus supervision signals. Extensive experiments on LLM alignment benchmarks demonstrate that RGPO effectively reduces inconsistency and noise in training data and achieves superior performance compared to widely adopted RLHF baselines. Our code and configurations are available at https://github.com/GenieHuang/RGPO.
